From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs (post-demo)

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really enjoyed the conversation and learning more about AcmeHealth's ingestion patterns. Per our ask from the call, a quick recap on what we store from prompts/outputs and how long: 

- Prompts (user-submitted text): by default Redwood stores full request payloads for up to 30 days to support debugging and replay. Customers can opt-in to extended retention for telemetry (30/90/365 days) or opt-out entirely for PII-sensitive workflows.
- Generated outputs (model responses): treated similarly to prompts — default 30-day retention. We can also offer non-persistent invocation modes where responses are not written to disk or logs.
- Structured metadata (request id, model version, timestamp, routing decisions): stored for 365 days by default to support billing and SLO analysis. These do not include prompt/output text unless explicitly enabled.

Residency & logging controls we discussed: 
- Hosted (default): data is stored in the region where your tenant is provisioned (we support US and EU regions).
- Dedicated / Private: for Dedicated deployments we can restrict both compute and storage to specific regions; for Private on-prem deployments customers control data residency entirely.
- Audit & access logs: access to stored prompts/outputs is logged; logs are retained based on the same retention policy but can be exported to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Log Analytics).

Attached is a short summary doc and a CSV mapping of retention defaults vs available options.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Neha to provide a short note confirming that prompt/output storage can be disabled for a scoped integration (Neha is cc'd).
2) Rishi to share the retention options + SOC2 basics (attached link).
3) If that looks good, we can put together a scoped technical plan for a PII-safe proof-of-concept (PoC) within your dev environment.

Happy to jump back on a quick call with your security team if helpful — propose Tue afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side before we share with InfoSec:

1) When you say "store full request payloads for up to 30 days" — can you confirm whether that includes any PII (SSNs, MRNs, PHI) that might be present in the prompt? Is there any automated redaction or detection?
2) For the non-persistent invocation mode, how is that enforced? Does that mode still write anything to ephemeral disk (e.g., for caching) that could be recovered?
3) If we choose Hosted US region, where exactly is data stored (AWS region names) and do you provide a data residency SLA?
4) For audit/access logs that contain request ids, can we configure log export to our Splunk instance within 24 hours?

Also, for the PoC we likely need a written confirmation that Redwood will not use any prompt or output content for model training or internal product analytics for this scoped integration. Can you have Neha or legal provide that in writing?

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs (post-demo)

Hi Erin —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Short answers up front, followed by the compliance-oriented detail you can share with InfoSec.

1) Prompts & PII: By default we do not scan or modify customer prompts for PII. That said, for scoped integrations we offer an optional PII-detection/redaction pipeline that can be enabled at ingestion. When enabled, the pipeline runs a deterministic tokenizer+pattern detector and produces a redacted prompt copy for storage; the original unredacted payload can be configured to not be persisted. Redaction patterns are configurable to match PHI classes (MRN, SSN) and custom regexes.

2) Non-persistent invocation mode: In this mode we route requests through memory-only processing and avoid writing prompt/output text to persistent storage. Ephemeral caching (in-memory KV) is used for tokenization and model runtime; nothing is written to disk. We do maintain minimal runtime telemetry (request id, latency, model version) which does not contain prompt/output text.

3) Hosted US region details: our US-hosted tenants store data in AWS us-west-2 (Oregon) by default; we can also provision us-east-1 on request. We provide a regional residency attestation for Dedicated customers and contractual language for Private deployments.

4) Log export: yes — we can configure push to your Splunk/S3 within 24 hours as part of the PoC. We also provide a signed S3 replication link for long-term archive if needed.

Training & analytics: Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs for model training or product analytics unless explicitly agreed in a contract. For PoC/scoped integrations we will include a clause that prohibits usage for training and analytics and confirms non-persistence of prompt/output text unless otherwise approved.

I've attached a one-page confirmation you can share with InfoSec and will follow up with a slightly expanded scoping template for the PoC that includes the redaction options and a checklist for controls.

Let me know if you'd like a 30-minute sync with our security engineering lead next week.

Thanks,
